title: Size of symmetric intersecting families in $[k]^n$
statement_text: How large can a symmetric, intersecting subfamily of $[k]^n$ really be (for fixed $k \geq 3$)?
context_text: Here $[k]^n$ is the set of vectors of length $n$ with entries in $[k]=\{1,\dots,k\}$, and $k\ge3$ is fixed while $n\to\infty$. A family $A\subseteq[k]^n$ is intersecting if any two of its vectors agree in at least one coordinate. The symmetric group $S_n$ acts on $[k]^n$ by permuting coordinates, and $A$ is symmetric if its automorphism group $\{\sigma\in S_n:\sigma(A)=A\}$ is transitive on $[n]$. Without symmetry the largest intersecting families have size $k^{n-1}$ (fix one coordinate). For $k=2$ and $n$ odd, the vectors with more $1$'s than $2$'s form an intersecting family of size $2^{n-1}$ invariant under all of $S_n$, but nothing similar happens for $k\ge3$: the authors prove that there is a universal $c>0$ such that every symmetric intersecting $A\subseteq[k]^n$ has $|A|=O(k^n/n^{c/k})$, in particular $|A|=o(k^n)$. A family $A$ is set-intersecting if there are a symmetric intersecting family $\mathcal{B}$ of subsets of $[n]$ (any two members meet, with transitive automorphism group) and $\ell\in[k]$ such that $x\in A$ if and only if $x_i=\ell$ for all $i\in B$, for some $B\in\mathcal{B}$; such $A$ is symmetric and intersecting. Taking $n=q^2+q+1$ with $q$ a prime power and $\mathcal{B}$ the lines of the projective plane $PG(2,q)$ gives size roughly $k^{n-\sqrt{n}}$, the best construction known to the authors. The authors describe determining the true maximum size as the most obvious question raised by their work. This is extremal set theory rather than graph theory.

title: Largest symmetric intersecting families are set-intersecting
statement_text: It seems possible (but maybe impossible to prove) that the largest symmetric intersecting families in $[k]^n$ are set-intersecting.

title: Polynomial improvement on symmetric intersecting family size bound
statement_text: Show that there exist constants $c, \delta > 0$ (possibly depending on $k$) such that for any symmetric intersecting $A \subset [k]^n$, we have $\log_k |A| \leq n - cn^{\delta}$.
context_text: Here $[k]^n$ is the set of vectors of length $n$ with entries in $[k]=\{1,\dots,k\}$, and $k\ge3$ is fixed while $n\to\infty$. A family $A\subseteq[k]^n$ is intersecting if any two of its vectors agree in at least one coordinate. The authors' bound gives $\log_k|A|\le n-\frac{c}{k}\log_k n+O(1)$, and the best construction has $\log_k|A|\approx n-\sqrt{n}$; failing a determination of the extremal families, they say it would be very interesting to at least obtain a polynomial gain $n^\delta$ in the exponent. This is extremal set theory rather than graph theory.
